exceptions.justification: `repo-contract affected` must run the project's OWN TypeScript (the compiler API it needs is the consumer's, version 6 or earlier), so the CLI resolves the literal module name "typescript" from the project directory with createRequire(<dir>/package.json). The specifier is a constant; nothing computed from input is ever loaded, and the loaded module is a build-time dependency the consumer already installed. Accepted as a risk rather than a false positive: the capability is real (a module is loaded at run time), bounded to one constant name, and reviewed here.
exceptions.alternatives: A static `import "typescript"` would load repo-contract's own copy, or fail when a project has none, instead of the project's compiler; an `import()` of the same literal has the same dynamic-load shape under this scan. Passing the compiler in through the library API (`repo-contract/affected` takes `ts` as an argument) is already how the library avoids this; the CLI is the one place that has to find it.
exceptions.remediation: Remove when TypeScript 7 ships a compiler API and the CLI can import a pinned dependency instead of the project's copy, or when the CLI is folded into a consumer-supplied runner.
